experiments.name: deepseek_mtp_spec_decode_tpot
experiments.workload: DeepSeek-R1 on 8x H200, tensor-parallel-size 8, MTP k=1 speculative decoding (draft TP=8); mean TPOT (time per output token) at QPS=1, baseline vs spec-decode. Acceptance rate ~81-82%.
experiments.note: Diff adds the DeepSeek MTP (multi-token-prediction) spec-decode path (new deepseek_mtp model + multi_step_worker/spec_decode wiring). Headline number is the draft-TP=8 QPS=1 row of the author's benchmark table in the PR body: baseline TPOT 55.47 ms -> k=1 TPOT 32.64 ms (1.69x). Draft TP=1 QPS=1 is 55.47->33.99 (1.63x). Speedup decays with QPS and goes <1.0x at QPS>=6.

reported.scope: end-to-end online-serving TPOT for DeepSeek-R1 across a full 8x H200 TP=8 deployment at QPS=1 (draft TP=8), not an isolated op
reported.scale_short: Author's number is whole-model E2E serving TPOT on 8x H200 with DeepSeek-R1; it is a system-level spec-decode win driven by token-acceptance, not a reproducible micro-op. Only QPS<=4 gains; QPS>=6 regresses. TO MAKE 1:1: serve DeepSeek-R1 TP=8 on 8x H200 with --num-speculative-tokens 1, drive QPS=1, and measure mean TPOT baseline vs MTP.
reported.scale_note: TPOT improvement comes from ~81-82% MTP draft acceptance shrinking decode steps; it depends on QPS, concurrency, and draft TP and cannot be isolated on a single CPU/GPU op. The table also shows the effect inverting (<1.0x) at QPS 6-8 as batching saturates, so the headline 1.69x is a low-load best case, not a uniform speedup.
